oneTimers: A $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations after the U.S. government required a license to export H20 products to China — sales of H20 chips were $4.6B in the quarter, and a further $2.5B of H20 revenue could not ship. Excluding the charge, non-GAAP gross margin would have been 71.3% (vs 60.5% GAAP) and diluted EPS $0.96 (vs $0.76 GAAP).

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $39.1B, up 73% — almost $89 of every $100 Nvidia took in — as Blackwell AI systems went into full production.
takeaways.title: Data Center is nearly the whole company

takeaways.text: A new U.S. license rule for H20 chips bound for China forced a $4.5B charge for unsold inventory and purchase commitments, and $2.5B of H20 sales that could not ship.
takeaways.title: The China export ban cost real money

takeaways.text: Excluding the H20 charge, gross margin would have been 71.3% and non-GAAP earnings $0.96 a share — the core AI business is still highly profitable.
takeaways.title: Underneath the charge, margins held up

verdict: Nvidia's revenue jumped 69% to $44.1B on AI data-center demand, but a $4.5B charge for H20 chips blocked from China cut gross margin to 60.5% — without it, earnings would have been $0.96 a share instead of $0.76.
